page: Amazon Web Services mac-m4pro.metal is a bare-metal macOS instance powered by a 14-core Apple arm64_mac processor running at a base clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 14 physical cores with one thread per core under a fully dedicated, non-hypervisor execution model. System memory measures 48.0 GB, yielding approximately 3.43 GB of memory per core.

Local hardware storage consists of an integrated 1900 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 10 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not include discrete GPU accelerators and supplies zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Standard x86 instruction sets and vector extensions such as AVX, AVX-512, and AMX are not present, reflecting the native Apple silicon system architecture.

Resource efficiency is concentrated in providing direct bare-metal access to Apple silicon without virtualization overhead. The combination of dedicated arm64 cores, 48.0 GB memory, and high-capacity NVMe storage is structured for macOS and iOS build automation, continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) pipelines, and application testing environments targeting the Apple software ecosystem.
description: Amazon Web Services mac-m4pro.metal is a bare-metal instance running macOS on an Apple 14-core arm64_mac processor clocked at 3.5 GHz. Each physical core corresponds to a single execution thread, providing non-virtualized dedicated compute capacity. The server integrates 48.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.43 GB per core, along with 1900 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage and a 10 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance features no discrete GPU coprocessors and lacks common x86 vector instruction extensions due to its native Apple silicon design. With its dedicated bare-metal model, mac-m4pro.metal delivers predictable performance for Apple-native software development pipelines, including continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD), macOS and iOS application compilation, and local automated test suites requiring direct access to Apple hardware and high-speed local storage.
